A Chicago man fatally struck another man walking on the shoulder of the Eisenhower Expressway and then drove off with the body still on his vehicle, prosecutors said in court on Monday. The body was still there when police pulled him over.

Circuit Court Judge Laura Sullivan set bail at $400,000 for Adrian Harris, 33, of the 5400 block of West Van Buren Street, charged with drunken driving and reckless homicide, during a hearing at the Leighton Criminal Court Building.

Harris is charged in the death of Jess Rodriguez, 41, who was walking on the shoulder of the Eisenhower Expressway early Saturday morning, the Chicago Tribune reported.

Prosecutors said the Rodriguez had gotten into an argument with his girlfriend, who got out of Rodriguez’s own vehicle around 3:51 a.m. near Western Avenue.

According to the charges, Rodriguez’s girlfriend was walking on the left shoulder on the Eisenhower Expressway. Rodriguez had pulled over to the right shoulder and got out of his car.

Rodriguez was attempting to cross the expressway to reach his girlfriend, according to witnesses in a van. Harris was driving behind the van and did not attempt to slow down when he drove around the van, striking Rodriguez, prosecutors said.

Prosecutors said that Harris blew a .169, more than twice the legal limit, the Tribune reported.

Rodriguez was pronounced dead of his injuries.

Illinois Department of Corrections records show that Harris is currently on parole stemming from a DUI conviction in 2014 and has six prior felony convictions.

Harris’s next court appearance is Oct. 23.

I bring you another tale from the gymnastics-coaching life. Our story today features a young boy whose mom couldn't control his eating habits, resulting in him now being overweight. I remember when I first came in about a month ago and saw him, the poor kid. He can't run nearly as fast or do the moves nearly as well. He requires a lot of manual assistance when trying to do moves. One example is handsprings into the foam pit, a move which most kids can do it by themselves practically on the first day. Literally getting on a trampoline, putting your hands on the edge, bouncing a few times and bringing your legs over your head like a handstand and falling off into the pit. I have to lift this kid's (very heavy) legs over his head for him and give him a little push so he goes forward. Another move he struggles with is pullovers, which is a bit more normal since they require a lot of getting used to. To help the kids, I have them put their chin and hands on the bar with their arms bent, take a couple steps forward, and kick up in the air for me to grab their legs and push them up and over the bar. However, this kid cannot even keep his arms bent long enough for me to get his hips over the bar. I have to literally grab his entire upper body along with his legs and essentially do all the work for him. He's like a very heavy ragdoll.

So last night one other coach and I were speaking to his mother, who appears to at least be bordering on overweight (she was wearing loose clothing so sort of tough to tell). She said she's trying to get him more active and help him lose weight so that he can perform gymnastics better. She told us he's getting frustrated to the point of wanting to quit. For his sake, I hope that his mom can learn how to control his intake before he just gives up completely. I can tell he just wants to perform to an average level like the rest of his peers, but I feel like if he quits gymnastics it will be game over for him.
